issues_detected.description: human_subject_research.involves_human_subjects is true for a dataset built from retrospective ICU, PICU and NICU hospital records, but no institutional ethics determination is recorded anywhere and there is no informed_consent slot at all. The record's own source_caveats state that the sources 'do not state an IRB approval, an ethics review board of record, or a regulatory compliance determination for the dataset'.
issues_detected.recommendation: Record the IRB determination or waiver of consent covering retrospective extraction at the 14 contributing hospitals, or state explicitly that the review is site-local and not published, so the absence reads as a documented fact rather than an omission.

issues_detected.description: ethical_reviews is populated with a single entry describing community-facing ethics focus groups, evaluation of community perspectives on clinical care AI, establishment of a legal framework, and analysis of the legal and regulatory landscape. That is community-engagement and policy work, not a review of this dataset by an ethics body. The slot is filled but its semantic content does not answer the slot's question.
issues_detected.recommendation: Move the focus-group and legal-landscape material to data_governance or future_use_impacts and reserve ethical_reviews for a named reviewing body and determination, keeping the source_caveats statement that none is published.

issues_detected.description: is_deidentified is populated with tokenization, re-identification-limiting transformation and imaging de-identification, but no de-identification standard is named for the structured OMOP data, participant_privacy.reidentification_risk is qualitative only ('no quantitative residual risk is reported'), and regulatory_restrictions carries no hipaa_compliant value for what is US hospital clinical data. The record declares each of these gaps rather than asserting a protection it cannot support.
issues_detected.recommendation: State the de-identification standard applied to the structured extract (Safe Harbor, Expert Determination, or a project-specific method) and the HIPAA posture of the enclave release.

issues_detected.description: at_risk_populations.at_risk_groups_included is true because PICU and NICU admissions are in the release, so minors and neonates are represented, yet no assent procedure, guardian consent, or special protection is documented and informed_consent is absent. The record marks the value as its own inference in source_caveats.
issues_detected.recommendation: Document the consent or waiver pathway for pediatric and neonatal records, or state that the sources describe none, so the true flag is paired with a protection statement.

issues_detected.description: license_and_use_terms names the MIT License for the chorus-ai GitHub code and no license at all for the data, while distribution_formats (5 modalities) and data_governance.access_review_process describe an active controlled-access release with a named access route. A dataset that is being distributed under a signed licensing agreement has terms that the record does not name.
issues_detected.recommendation: Name the data use agreement governing enclave access, distinct from the MIT license covering the software; the caveat correctly separates them but leaves the data terms unnamed.

issues_detected.description: id is 'https://chorus4ai.org/', byte-identical to page. The record's identifier is therefore the project homepage rather than a dataset identifier, and no doi is present. A sibling CHORUS record at least distinguished the two with a '#dataset' fragment.
issues_detected.recommendation: Mint a distinct dataset id (a fragment on the project URI at minimum) and record a DOI if one exists, so that id, page and doi are three separate claims.

issues_detected.description: The external_resources entry 'www.bridge2ai.org/chorus' carries no URI scheme, so it is not a resolvable URL as written. It is transcribed as printed in the GitHub organization contact section.
issues_detected.recommendation: Record the resolvable form (https://www.bridge2ai.org/chorus) and keep the as-printed string in notes if verbatim transcription matters.

issues_detected.description: The maintainer contact email is recorded as 'cmccrary@mgh.havard.edu', with a source_caveats entry stating that the domain is transcribed exactly as printed on chorus4ai.org and that the source does not indicate whether it is a typographical error. The transcription discipline is correct, but the contact as recorded does not resolve to a real domain.
issues_detected.recommendation: Keep the verbatim value and the caveat, and add the probable corrected domain as a separate annotated field rather than silently repairing it.

issues_detected.description: instances[0].counts is 50000 with no uncertainty marker at the value, while the top-level source_caveats records that the cohort-2 webinar states 'over 45K unique admissions' as of August 2025. The disagreement is disclosed and the manifest-rank tie-break is explained, but a consumer reading only the structured count sees one figure.
issues_detected.recommendation: Carry the competing figure into the instance-level notes as well as the top-level caveat, so the disagreement travels with the value.

issues_detected.description: known_biases and future_use_impacts are both absent, yet the bias content exists in substance elsewhere: known_limitations carries a representativeness_limitation stating that no demographic, geographic or clinical distribution is reported for the released cohort, and participant_privacy.notes describes managing 'privacy and bias while accounting for social determinants of health'. The material is present but not in the slots a bias taxonomy would be read from.
issues_detected.recommendation: Promote the representativeness statement into a typed known_biases entry with a bias_type term and a mitigation_strategy, and record the holdout-set and marketplace-adoption material as future_use_impacts.

issues_detected.description: conforms_to_standard uses the OTHER enum value three times (top level, the tokenized-notes collection, and the EEG collection) where the vocabulary has no term for OHNLP, EDF+ or Persyst. The fallback is used correctly and the prose conforms_to recovers the specific standard, but the structured value alone loses the information.
issues_detected.recommendation: No record-level change needed; this is a vocabulary coverage gap worth raising against the enum rather than against this datasheet.

issues_detected.description: status is 'partially released' and access_review_process describes a live access route, but there is no version, no version_access, no errata and no release cadence. updates.source_caveats states that the sources give no versioning policy. A released artefact with an active access path has no versioning anchor a user could cite.
issues_detected.recommendation: Record the release identifier used inside the enclave, or state that releases are unversioned and cite the August 2025 snapshot date as the only temporal anchor.

semantic_insights: Grant number OT2OD032701 follows the NIH pattern correctly (activity code OT2, institute OD, serial 032701), and the RePORTER project-details identifier 10472824 in external_resources matches the application ID recorded in the funders note. Award amount and 2022-09-01 to 2026-11-30 period are internally consistent.

Temporal ordering is coherent throughout: award period 2022-09-01 to 2026-11-30, dataset snapshot August 2025, cohort-2 webinar September 2025, and training-program dates (call 2025-09-02, notice of award 2025-11-10, start 2025-11-17). The record explicitly refuses to read the award period as the clinical encounter period, which is the correct distinction.

The record separates planned from released capability with discipline. The holdout test set appears in splits, tasks and intended_uses, each carrying a source_caveats entry stating that the award abstract describes it prospectively and that no size or availability is reported. existing_uses similarly demotes the prospective cohort-2 curriculum to intended_uses with a reason.

The five distribution_formats map one-to-one onto five file_collections and onto the typed instances, and each modality carries the same access posture (controlled) across all three places. Modality-level consistency across composition, distribution and conformance is complete.

The two source disagreements are surfaced rather than reconciled: 50,000 admissions versus 'over 45K unique admissions', and 7,642 admissions with radiology versus roughly 1,000 images. The record names the manifest rank that decided the first and explains that the second pair are different units, which is the right treatment for a genuine unit mismatch.

The record declares a transcription artefact in the source itself: the webinar's data inventory table is rendered with columns partially separated in the extracted text, so data-type-to-standard pairings are stated only where unambiguous. That is a legible limit on what the record claims, not a hedge.

Tokenization as a de-identification approach is semantically appropriate for free-text clinical notes, and the design decision that note text never leaves the contributing site is recorded consistently in description, instances, confidential_elements, raw_data_sources and known_limitations.

No DOI is asserted. Given that the dataset is controlled-access inside an enclave with no repository deposit, the absence is plausible rather than an omission of a known identifier, but it costs the record on findability and sustainability.

correctness_validations.url_validity: id, page, chorus4ai.org, github.com/chorus-ai, reporter.nih.gov and the aim-ahead.net webinar PDF are well-formed and plausible; one external_resources entry 'www.bridge2ai.org/chorus' lacks a URI scheme; the maintainer email domain 'mgh.havard.edu' is a source-side misspelling, transcribed verbatim with a declared caveat

Absent: prohibited_uses, discouraged_uses, future_use_impacts.
questions.quality_note: Intended uses are concrete, categorised and each tied to a source, and the use terms are stated as enforceable conditions, which meets the middle anchor. Everything above it is missing: no license is named for the data itself, prohibited and discouraged uses are entirely absent for a controlled-access clinical dataset where misuse boundaries matter, and there is no social impact analysis, risk identification or mitigation content anywhere — future_use_impacts is unpopulated, so the only downstream-impact material (holdout provisioning for marketplace adoption) sits in purposes and tasks instead.

questions.name: Data Integrity, Provenance Graph, and Quality
questions.description: Version access, errata, updates, derivation, parent datasets, splits, missing data
questions.score_label: Substantially complete textual lineage; no version history or structured graph
questions.evidence: was_derived_from: clinical source systems at the 14 contributing hospitals, naming EHRs, PACS archives, bedside monitors with gateway/middleware and hospital EEG databases. raw_data_sources (5) with source_type, raw_data_format and access_details per modality. Activities are traceable through acquisition_methods (observation, derivation, validation), preprocessing_strategies (OMOP mapping, OHNLP tokenization, waveform conversion) and cleaning_strategies (characterization reports, validated mappings under a clinical validation SOP). Agents are named in data_collectors (site data managers, Data Acquisition centers, Standards/Data Acquisition/Tooling sub-teams). instances carry two missing_information entries with why_missing (imaging beyond ~1,000 images pending de-identification; full note text retained on site). splits and updates present. Absent: version_access, errata, parent_datasets, missing_data_documentation as its own slot, subsets.is_data_split.
questions.quality_note: Entity, activity and agent are all recoverable as text and the derivation path is traceable per modality from hospital system through mapping, tokenization or conversion to the controlled release — the question accepts textual provenance, and this is more than the middle anchor describes. was_derived_from is explicit rather than implied, and missing data is documented with reasons at instance level. The top anchor is missed because there is no version history at all to integrate with the lineage, no errata or version_access, no parent_datasets linkage, and the relationships are prose a reader must assemble rather than a structured graph a tool could traverse.

questions.name: Bias Documentation and Responsible AI Alignment
questions.applicability_evidence: Not gated by the sharing condition: a dataset that is never released still has documentable biases.
questions.description: Known biases with standard taxonomy and fairness analysis
questions.score_label: Bias touched only obliquely, outside the bias slots
questions.evidence: known_biases absent. future_use_impacts absent. The nearest content sits elsewhere: known_limitations includes a representativeness_limitation stating that data come from 14 hospitals drawn from 20 academic centres and that no demographic, geographic or clinical distribution achieved in the release is reported; sampling_strategies records an intent that federated access enable 'a balanced and diverse cohort' with a caveat that the applied sampling is unreported; participant_privacy.notes mentions patient-focused efforts to 'manage privacy and bias while accounting for social determinants of health'; addressing_gaps aspires to 'the most diverse, high-resolution, ethically sourced, AI-ready data set'.
questions.quality_note: No bias is identified as a bias. There is no typed entry, no taxonomy term, no BiasTypeEnum or AIO mapping, no mitigation strategy recorded as such, and no fairness analysis of the released cohort. The representativeness limitation and the diversity aspiration are real signals that a bias entry could have been built from, and their presence keeps this above zero, but a consumer looking for documented bias in the fields where bias is recorded finds nothing. This is the record's weakest question and a clear regression against sibling CHORUS records that populate known_biases.

strengths: Funding and attribution are complete and format-valid: one NIH Common Fund grant (OT2OD032701) with full RePORTER award metadata, and six named investigators with institutional affiliations, each attributed to the document that names them.

Modality coverage is internally consistent across the record: five distribution formats map one-to-one onto five described file collections and onto six typed instance entries, with the same controlled-access posture and the same conformance declaration repeated at each level.

Provenance reads as a traceable textual lineage rather than a list: was_derived_from names the source systems, raw_data_sources types each one, preprocessing and acquisition describe the transforming activities, and data_collectors name the agents who perform them.

The record separates what is released from what is planned, with a source caveat attached at each point — the holdout test set, the annotation environment, the cohort-2 curriculum and the EEG and imaging pipelines are all marked prospective rather than presented as available.

Genuine source disagreements are surfaced instead of reconciled away: the 50,000 versus 45K admission counts, the 7,642 imaging admissions versus roughly 1,000 available images, and a garbled table in the extracted webinar text are each recorded with the reason the record did not resolve them.
weaknesses: Bias documentation is effectively absent: known_biases and future_use_impacts are both unpopulated, so no bias is typed, no taxonomy term is used, no mitigation is recorded and no fairness analysis of the released cohort exists, despite the material for one sitting in known_limitations.

The dataset carries no version, no version_access, no errata, no DOI, no publisher and no repository of deposit, so there is nothing a user could cite or return to; status 'partially released' and an ongoing-acquisition narrative are the only anchors.

The ethics documentation names no review of record, and the one populated ethical_reviews entry describes community focus groups and legal-landscape analysis rather than an ethics determination; informed_consent is absent entirely for a cohort the record states includes minors and neonates.

No license is named for the data. The only license named is MIT on the GitHub code, and the access terms described belong to one training-programme registration route rather than a general data use agreement.

Human subject representation is by care setting only. There is no age, sex, race, ethnicity or comorbidity distribution, no inclusion or exclusion criteria, and no per-site or per-setting breakdown of the 50,000 admissions, which the record's own representativeness limitation acknowledges.
recommendations: Populate known_biases with at least a typed representativeness entry built from the existing known_limitations text, giving a bias_type term, a bias_description covering the 14-of-20-centre catchment and the unreported cohort distribution, and the federated-sampling intent as an explicit mitigation_strategy; record the holdout and marketplace-adoption material as future_use_impacts.

Give the dataset an identity distinct from its landing page: mint an id separate from page, record a DOI if one exists, and name the publisher or repository of record; add a version identifier for the current release even if it is only the August 2025 snapshot date.

Record the ethics pathway that actually governs the extraction — the IRB determination, waiver of consent, or a statement that reviews are site-local and unpublished — and move the focus-group and legal-framework content to data_governance so ethical_reviews answers its own question.

Name the data use agreement governing enclave access as license_and_use_terms for the data, kept distinct from the MIT license on the code, and add prohibited_uses and discouraged_uses, which a controlled-access critical care dataset needs and currently lacks entirely.

Add whatever demographic characterization the sources support for the released 50,000 admissions, or state explicitly that none is published, and add the per-setting ICU, PICU and NICU split if it becomes available, since the subpopulation entries currently exist without any figure attached.
